Abegweit First Nation

Abegweit First Nation is a Mi’kmaq community on Epekwitk (Prince Edward Island). The Nation names three communities that make up Abegweit: Morell, Rocky Point and Scotchfort. Its headquarters are in Scotchfort.

01

Three communities on Epekwitk

Abegweit’s account of its history dates the formation of its band government to 1972. The Nation names Morell, Rocky Point and Scotchfort as its three communities. A joint announcement by Abegweit, Canada and Prince Edward Island lists their numbered reserve names as Morell 2, Rocky Point 3 and Scotchfort 4.

Read the sources [1] Abegweit First Nation [4] Indigenous Services Canada, Abegweit First Nation, and the Province of Prince Edward Island

02

A community hatchery in Scotchfort

Abegweit’s Fisheries and Natural Resources program identifies stream enhancement and conservation as part of its work. In Scotchfort, the Abegweit Biodiversity Enhancement Hatchery raises brook trout and Atlantic salmon to stock Island rivers. The hatchery dates its start to 2012. Its education work introduces younger generations to the Island fishery and ways to help preserve it.

Read the sources [2] Abegweit First Nation [3] Abegweit Biodiversity Enhancement Hatchery

03

Planning for emergencies

On May 4, 2026, Abegweit First Nation, Canada and Prince Edward Island announced an agreement to coordinate emergency management. The announcement describes joint planning and training for emergencies that affect the community.

Read the sources [4] Indigenous Services Canada, Abegweit First Nation, and the Province of Prince Edward Island

What needs further research

  • Further reading could trace the histories of Morell, Rocky Point and Scotchfort through accounts from each community.

First Nation community accountAbegweit First NationSource 1

Who We Are ↗

The Nation introduces itself as a Mi’kmaq community in Epekwitk (Prince Edward Island), lists three reserve communities, and dates the formation of its band government to 1972.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Page heading and selected self-description, distinct founding date and three place names on lines 67, 69, 73–74. The date applies to the band government; the earlier continuity, disputed age estimates, present leaders, affiliate relationships and territories are outside the selected account.

Review recorded: November 19, 2026

Abegweit First Nation, the Government of Canada, and the Province of Prince Edward Island announce a first-of-its-kind multilateral emergency management agreement ↗

Publication: 2026-05-04

The May 4, 2026 news release identifies the Nation’s headquarters in Scotchfort and names Morell 2, Rocky Point 3 and Scotchfort 4. It describes an agreement to coordinate emergency planning, training and preparedness.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Named publication parties and publication date, announced agreement and planning purpose, and the headquarters/three named reserves in lines 23–38, 64 and 106. Legal interpretation, implementation, individual officeholders, population, language translation, boundaries and funding were outside scope.

Review recorded: November 19, 2026
